title: Chemistry of the Atmosphere
seo_title: Year 11 Science: Chemistry of the Atmosphere Worksheets (GCSE Combined Science)
standard_code: KS4 Chemistry: Chemistry of the atmosphere
standard_text: The proportions of different gases in the atmosphere; the Earth's early atmosphere and how it evolved; how oxygen increased and carbon dioxide decreased; greenhouse gases and human activities; global climate change; the carbon footprint and its reduction; atmospheric pollutants from fuels and their properties and effects.
meta_desc: Free Year 11 GCSE Combined Science worksheets on the atmosphere: the gases in air, the early atmosphere, greenhouse gases, climate change, carbon footprints and air pollutants. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Air is about four-fifths nitrogen and one-fifth oxygen.
key_sub: Greenhouse gases absorb heat radiated by the Earth.
body_html:
How to think about it

Earth's atmosphere has changed over billions of years.

  • The early atmosphere was mainly carbon dioxide from volcanoes. Algae and plants added oxygen.
  • Carbon dioxide, methane and water vapour are greenhouse gases. Burning fuels and farming increase them.
  • Pollutants: carbon monoxide (toxic), sulfur dioxide and oxides of nitrogen (acid rain), particulates (global dimming).
Example

0.17 kg CO₂ per km, 50 km?

0.17 × 50

Answer: 8.5 kg

Example

Which gas is about 80% of air?

Four-fifths

Answer: nitrogen

Common mistakes

  • Thinking air is mostly oxygen.
  • Thinking nitrogen is a greenhouse gas.
  • Thinking carbon monoxide causes acid rain.

faq.q: How did the early atmosphere change?
faq.a: Volcanoes released carbon dioxide and water vapour. The water formed oceans. Algae and plants made oxygen, and carbon dioxide was locked in rocks and fossil fuels.
Carbon dioxide, methane and water vapour. They absorb long-wavelength radiation from the Earth and keep it warm.

faq.q: Which pollutants come from burning fuels?
faq.a: Carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide, soot (particulates), sulfur dioxide and oxides of nitrogen.
